sessions.title: One minute of breathing
sessions.transcript: This is one minute, just for you. There's no right way to do it. If it feels okay, let your shoulders drop a little. Breathe in slowly. And let it out, a little longer than it came in. Again. In. And out. If your mind wanders, that's what minds do. Notice where it went, and come back. In. And out. Whatever you're carrying is still here, and so are you. That's enough for one minute. If things feel like too much, Get help now is at the top of the screen, any time.

sessions.title: Notice five things
sessions.transcript: This is a few minutes to land where you are. You can keep your eyes open. Look around, and find five things you can see. Just name them to yourself. A color. A shape. Something small you didn't notice before. Now four things you can feel. Your feet on the floor. The weight of your hands. The air on your skin. Three things you can hear. Near, or far away. You don't have to like them, only notice them. Two things you can smell, or just the air as you breathe in. And one slow breath. Your mind may still be busy. If a thought shows up, you might quietly say to yourself, there's a thought. Then come back to what's here. Notice that you can carry a hard thought and still be in this room, in this moment. One more look around. What's one thing here you'd like to remember? That's it. You can come back to this any time you need to land. If things feel like too much, Get help now is at the top of the screen, any time.

sessions.title: Setting the day down
sessions.transcript: This is a few minutes to set the day down before you sleep. Get comfortable, however that looks for you. Let your breath find its own pace. You don't need to change it. Notice where your body meets the bed, or the chair. Let it hold a little more of your weight. Bring your attention to your feet, and let them be heavy. Your legs. Your back, and your shoulders. Your hands, and your jaw. If they're tight, that's okay. Just notice. Thoughts about today, or tomorrow, may come up. That's what a busy mind does at night. When one shows up, you might name it gently. Planning. Worrying. Remembering. And let it sit at the edge, like a phone on the other side of the room. You don't have to solve anything tonight. Think of one thing from today that mattered to you, even a small one. A conversation. Something you tried. Something you got through. Let that be the last thing you hold before you rest. Breathe in. And out, slowly. Sleep well. And if tonight feels like too much, Get help now is at the top of the screen, any time.
